Page tokens: {dur} {curator_dur} {curator_mult} {collectors_list} {collectors_pieces} {both_dur} {party1} {party2} {fiend} {fiend_pct} {carn} {carn_super} {herb} {herb_super} {classfreak} {count}. Note tokens (per item): {fx0} first buff's number, {perkpct:PERK_EDID} how much the perk changes it in %, {mgefpct:MGEF_EDID} that effect's magnitude in %, {mgefx:MGEF_EDID} 1 / (1 - magnitude). Notes: ["note" | "bug", text], keyed by the item's EDID (Glowing bobbleheads use the normal one's note). guides: {"id": guide_index id} or {"children_of": parent id, "strip": [title prefixes to cut]}. perkbar: which perks the finder's perk bar shows (curator, collectors, party, fiend, sin, classfreak).

alcohol.title: Buffs - Alcohol Buffs
alcohol.blurb: Every beer, spirit and wine and what it really does, straight from the game files. Find the best drink for your build, compare up to three side by side, or open any drink for its buffs, side effects and when it works.
basics: Most drinks have a chance to make you addicted to alcohol. The chance is shown with each drink.
Party Boy / Party Girl (Luck) multiplies the good effects of alcohol: ×{party1} at rank 1, ×{party2} at the top rank.
Drinks with the same kind of buff replace each other. Drinks with different buffs stack.

Some drinks leave you with a hangover when they wear off. The Rad Ant Lager and Hard Lemonade hangovers are cleared by your next alcoholic drink. The Mild Hangover (Lead Champagne, Tick Blood Tequila, Ballistic Bock, Hoppy Hunter, High Voltage Hefe, White Russian, Toxic Gin, Firecracker Whiskey and Appalachian Bubbly) and the Nukashine hangover are not: drinking again doesn't clear them, they just run out.

Brew_RadAntLager: When it wears off you get a hangover that takes {fx0} lb off your carry weight. Your next alcoholic drink clears the hangover, so drink again before it ends and you keep the +{fx0} lb going without ever losing it.
Brew_LemonadeHard: When it wears off you get a Sugar Crash hangover that lowers your Action Points and AP regen. Your next alcoholic drink clears it.

chems.count: There are currently {count} chems and serums.

food.title: Buffs - Food Buffs
food.blurb: Every food, drink, tea, juice, sweet and gum and what it really does, straight from the game files. Find the best food for your build, compare up to three side by side, or open any dish for its buffs, side effects and when it works.
food.count: There are currently {count} foods and drinks.
basics: Carnivore doubles the buffs from meat dishes (×{carn}, ×{carn_super} with Strange In Numbers in a team) and takes away the buffs from vegetable dishes.
Herbivore doubles the buffs from vegetable, herb and fruit dishes (×{herb}, ×{herb_super} with Strange In Numbers in a team) and takes away the buffs from meat dishes.
Herb and fruit dishes are Hybrid: a Carnivore still gets the normal buff, and a Herbivore gets it doubled.
Dishes with the same kind of buff replace each other. Dishes with different buffs stack.
Rad-X stops your mutations while it lasts, so Carnivore and Herbivore stop working too.

ATX_TeaWizard_LuckyLeaf: Its Luck has its own slot, so it stacks with your usual Luck food: eat both. In a team it adds more Luck for every teammate, up to a full team of four.
ATX_VaultTecGelatinCake_CakeSlice: Its Charisma shares a slot with other Charisma food, so the one you eat last replaces the other. The extra Charisma you get in a team counts as a chem buff: eating the cake removes the chem you have running, and taking a chem removes the team Charisma. So you can't keep the team Charisma and a chem going at the same time.

bobbleheads.title: Buffs - Bobblehead Buffs
bobbleheads.blurb: Every bobblehead and what it really does, straight from the game files. Find the best one for your build, compare up to three side by side, or open any bobblehead for what it does, which weapons it works with and when it works.
bobbleheads.count: There are currently {count} bobbleheads (plus the Glowing versions, which do exactly the same).
basics: Every bobblehead lasts {dur}.
The Curator perk card (Intelligence) makes it last {curator_dur}.
Collector's legendary armour adds time for every piece you wear: {collectors_list}.
With Curator and {collectors_pieces} pieces of Collector's it lasts {both_dur} (we haven't confirmed in game that the two stack).
You can only have one bobblehead active. Using another one (Glowing ones included) replaces it.
It stacks with food, a chem, a drink and your magazine.
Glowing bobbleheads do exactly the same as the normal ones.

Bobblehead_Repair_Potion: The game says fusion cores last {perkpct:Bobblehead_RepairPerk}% longer, but that part only works on a Gatling Laser's fusion cores. It also does something the description doesn't mention: Power Armour drains its fusion core {mgefpct:Bobblehead_ReducePABatteryDamageRate_Effect}% slower, so a core lasts about {mgefx:Bobblehead_ReducePABatteryDamageRate_Effect} times as long.

Magazine_GunsAndBullets07_Potion: The game says +{fx0}% Unscoped Weapon Damage, but in the game files this magazine has no weapon check at all, so it boosts every weapon you use: scoped, melee and thrown too. A bug report has been sent to Bethesda.
Magazine_LiveAndLove05_Potion: Its Luck buff only works while you have a drink active (any beer, spirit or wine). Drinking doesn't remove the magazine.
Magazine_AwesomeTales03_Potion: The Health Regen only works while you are swimming. Breathe Underwater works all the time. The pickup message says you swim faster, but the game files give health regen while swimming instead.
Magazine_Backwoodsman07_Potion: The game says -{fx0}% disease chance from food and drink, but the game files only cut it by {perkpct:Magazine_Backwoodsman07Perk}%. A bug report has been written for Bethesda.

mutations.title: Buffs - Mutation Buffs
mutations.blurb: Every mutation and what it really does, good and bad, straight from the game files. Find the best mutations for your build, compare up to three side by side, or open any mutation for its buffs, its downsides and when they work.
basics: Mutations last until you cure them (RadAway can remove them unless you have Starched Genes).
Class Freak (Luck) makes the bad effects smaller: {classfreak}.
Strange In Numbers (Charisma) makes the good effects stronger while you are in a team with another mutated player.
Rad-X stops all your mutations, good and bad, while it lasts.
A serum gives you the mutation.
